name: Gulshan
tagline: Embassies, lake views and the city's serviced apartments
description: Dhaka's diplomatic and business quarter, built on a numbered road grid around Gulshan lake, with embassies, corporate towers, supermarkets and the best hotels. It has the widest streets, the most reliable power and the most English spoken anywhere in the city. Almost every foreign resident starts here.
bestFor: Remote workers who want reliable power, fast internet and international-standard services above all else.
pros: Most dependable electricity and internet in Dhaka
Serviced apartments, supermarkets and clinics geared to foreigners
Lakeside walking paths and wider roads
cons: By far the most expensive rents in the country
Gridlock on the Gulshan avenues most of the day
Feels like a bubble, detached from the rest of Dhaka

name: Banani
tagline: Rooftop restaurants and offices on road 11
description: Immediately north of Gulshan and busier at street level, Banani stacks cafes, rooftop restaurants and small offices into mid-rise buildings around road 11. Younger professionals and returning Bangladeshi expats live here. Rents sit slightly under Gulshan while keeping the same shops and services within reach.
bestFor: Nomads who want Gulshan's convenience with more street life and slightly lower rent.
pros: Best cafe and restaurant density in north Dhaka
Cheaper than Gulshan while sharing its amenities
Walking distance to Gulshan offices and the airport road
cons: Very noisy, constant horns on road 11
Traffic and construction dust are relentless

name: Dhanmondi
tagline: Lake-side older Dhaka, universities, bookshops and coaching centres
description: A settled residential area in the west built around the Dhanmondi lake, full of universities, cultural centres, bookshops and long-standing family apartment blocks. It has the most walkable lakefront in Dhaka and a strong cafe culture aimed at students. Rents are well below the Gulshan side.
bestFor: Long stayers who want cultural life, lake walks and a much lower rent than the diplomatic zone.
pros: Clearly cheaper than Gulshan or Banani
Lakeside paths, cafes and cultural venues
Deep local character and good street food
cons: Power cuts are more frequent than in Gulshan

name: Bashundhara Residential Area
tagline: Planned blocks, new apartments and a big student population
description: A large master-planned district on the eastern edge, laid out in lettered blocks with wide roads, newer apartment buildings and North South University at its heart. It is calmer and cleaner than inner Dhaka, with the country's biggest shopping mall nearby, and rent per square metre is reasonable.
bestFor: Nomads who want a modern, spacious flat and calmer streets, and do not mind being out of the centre.
pros: Newer buildings with lifts and backup generators
Good value space compared with Gulshan
cons: Long, unpredictable commute into central Dhaka
Still under construction in many blocks, so dust and noise
Low-lying land, some blocks flood in heavy rain

name: Uttara
tagline: Sector-numbered suburb by the airport with metro access
description: A self-contained northern suburb organised into numbered sectors, with parks, lakes, schools and its own restaurants and malls. The Dhaka metro terminates here, which makes trips south far more predictable than by road. It is the quietest option for anyone happy to live away from the business districts.
bestFor: Budget-minded long stayers and families who value quiet, space and metro access over central location.
pros: Metro line makes journeys south predictable
Noticeably cheaper and quieter than Gulshan
Parks, lakes and a self-contained set of services
cons: Far from Gulshan and the CBD if you travel by road
Aircraft noise on approach paths near the airport
Nightlife and international options are thin
